_about: THE SHRINKING OFFENDER LIST for `make docs-audit`'s `typed interpunct` row (D218; D280, which retires D218's pinned count). files: file -> lane (who owes the fix) and `interpunct` -> every user-visible string in that file that types a middle dot or bullet, exactly as scripts/user-strings.mjs (--join-literals --include-code-attr) extracts it, once per occurrence. An entry is `<scope>: <string>`, where scope is the named function, class, arrow binding or module-level constant around the string, so one entry excuses one string in one place and never the same string typed elsewhere in the file. Growth is counted per file (a file git renamed maps to its old path), by the string without its scope, so a renamed function's entries are re-keyed by hand and are not growth. The row FAILS on a typed dot this list does not name, on an entry that matches nothing (stale: delete it), and on an entry the list at the merge-base with origin/main did not hold (growth). A lane that fixes a string deletes its entry in the same commit. `make offenders-prune` does that delete and never adds an entry. Never add an entry to excuse a new dot: build the parts as elements and let CSS draw the separator (D41).
